definition.usefulBidirectionalJourney: A user reaches a different civic context and can return without losing identity or scope.
definition.redundantLoop: A link sends the user to another surface that adds no material context, or merely routes them back to the same generic domain.

decisions.reason: Generic Accountability, Legislation and Public Records indexes implied office-specific relationships that the graph did not support.
Title search was an indirect loop-prone way to rediscover a known timeline item.
decisions.replacement: Exact timeline-item anchor by timeline ID.

decisions.reason: Repeated BetterGov/BetterLGU destinations could drift and obscured their context-only evidence role.
The links were specifically Accountability entries, so the generic label overstated the record family.

The economy section offers indicator-relevant national data continuations; the footer offers broader page-level national datasets, visualizations and benchmarks. The two placements answer different next questions.
Top quick actions are task entry points; the later civic-information section is a domain-oriented hub on a long local homepage. Repeated destinations are separated by purpose and scroll distance.
Election results provide race context while the official profile provides office/profile context. Exact anchors prevent a generic bounce.
The report owns the analysis while Calendar owns the time-axis view. Exact timeline anchors make the round trip meaningful.
The ledger explains the public record; the Civic Asset supplies place context. Typed record anchors preserve the return journey.
About provides broad ecosystem orientation. Domain pages expose only task-specific national context. BetterLGU remains on About rather than being repeated generically.
